label: current
workload: llama-cli -m Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf -p 'The capital of France is' -n 128 --ignore-eos --temp 0 --seed 42 --reasoning off -ngl 99 --single-turn (decode-dominated: 6-token prompt + 128 generated tokens)
method: in-app op-level SYCL device timers (GGML_SYCL_PROFILE=1): ctx->stream().wait() bracketed around each op's dispatch in ggml_backend_sycl_graph_compute, accumulated by ggml_op_desc() and dumped cumulatively at the end of every graph_compute call. This is a documented sycl-profiler SS5 fallback: unitrace (both overview and slice modes, with and without --call-logging) segfaults deterministically during model load on this runner, independent of workload size (confirmed on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-0.6B alike; see .sycl/state/lessons.md). The per-op wait() forces serialization, so this is a ranking tool (relative op share), not an absolute-latency benchmark -- op overlap/pipelining possible on the real (unsynced) path is not reflected.

ranking.notes: Q8_0-weight x F32-activation matmul, dequantize-then-oneMKL-GEMM path (mmf.cpp/dequantize.cpp), deliberately correctness-first per the migrate-phase brief; quantized-native MMA was explicitly deferred to this optimize phase. Decode-dominated workload (batch=1 steps) routes through mmvq; mmq (batched/prefill) contributes a smaller share of the 6-token prompt pass. Top optimization target.
Decode-dominated workload uses the single-query vec flash-attention kernel; F16-only KV cache per this model's config. Second-largest optimization target.
